root_cause.text: The `NPU_SET_IFM_REGION` handler in the Ethos-U NPU command stream parser applies an incorrect bitmask (`0x7f`) to the input parameter, allowing region indices up to 127 to be written into arrays sized only for 8 elements.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies `drivers/accel/ethosu/ethosu_gem.c` to change `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;` to `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7;`, correcting an inconsistency with other region handlers since `region_size[]` and `output_region[]` in `struct ethosu_validated_cmdstream_info` are limited to `NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX` (8).

candidates.rationale: This statement applies the incorrect bitmask 0x7f (allowing values up to 127) to the input parameter instead of the correct 3-bit mask 0x7 (allowing values up to 7). This permits region indices outside the valid range of 0-7 to be written into the structure, leading to potential out-of-bounds array access given the array size is only 8 elements.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement applies the incorrect bitmask 0x7f (binary: 1111111) which allows region indices up to 127 to be written. However, the NPU hardware only supports 3-bit region indices (0-7), and the corresponding array is sized for only 8 elements. This mismatch permits out-of-bounds array access when region values > 7 are used, potentially causing memory corruption or privilege escalation.
